In 2024, Character AI said it was answering 20,000 messages a second, around a fifth of what Google Search handled.

In September 2025, Disney’s lawyers ordered it to pull every Disney character off the app.

Last month, ex-CEO Karandeep Anand left to become Disney’s CTO, and some of his staff went with him.

On Monday, Character AI filed for bankruptcy.

Now, Disney is bidding $20M to license parts of Character AI’s tech, and those ex-employees will help keep the app running during the sale.

Other buyers can still outbid Disney before the auction wraps. If nobody steps in, the company says it will shut down.

Grok Bot can now claim its own email address, so we tested it with several project emails, one of which changed a deadline.

It caught the new date, summarized what changed, and drafted a reply marked "Needs approval."

Here’s how to try it:

-> Ask your Grok Bot to claim an address in the desktop app

-> Send it a few project updates from an account you control

-> Ask what changed and what’s still unanswered

-> Have it draft one reply, and check every recipient before anything sends

NEW: Meta released Muse Wonder (codenamed Watermelon), its new family of AI models, with scores that push the company to the frontier.

The top version, Wonder Full, scores 56 on Artificial Analysis’ Intelligence Index, behind only Claude Opus 5.5 at 58.

It also leads rivals on:

- Legal work (Harvey LAB): 13.1 vs. 8.6 for GPT-6 Astra
- Long coding projects (SWE-Marathon): 57.5 vs. 46.3 for Opus 5.5
- Coding tasks (DeepSWE): 79.0 vs. 74.2 for Opus 5.5
- Remembering context (MemoryBench): 85.5 vs. 81.5 for Opus 5.5

Muse Wonder is live today in the Meta Model API and Muse Code, with Wonder Full open to paying Muse Code users.

The paper-trail detective

Marty rebuilt 20+ years of scattered professional work, including 250+ records recovered from old publications, broken links, and archives.

Every find gets sorted as verified, probable, or rejected, same-name strangers get ruled out, and missing years stay marked as gaps instead of getting made up.

The one-person record label

Adriana built a full music release pipeline out of AI tools: lyrics and mood in ChatGPT, the track in Suno, cover art from ChatGPT, and the video cut in Clipchamp.

A ChatGPT agent handles the downloads and archiving. Then each song ships to YouTube, TikTok, Facebook, LinkedIn, and X.

Credit to Adriana Pausenwein: https://t.co/GjMD48CGF0

The add-on bouncer

Patrick built agent-guard, a free tool that checks the add-ons you give AI agents like Claude Code and Codex for malware and password theft before they install.

It runs security scanners from NVIDIA, Cisco, and Datadog, returns a plain safe-or-blocked verdict, and installs only the exact version it checked.

Credit to Patrick Illian: https://t.co/6uzLuSuNJY

The ruin hunter

Gil turned a month of unused ChatGPT tokens into an archaeology dig.

A team of agents on Raft scans LiDAR maps of dense Slovenian forest for anything that looks man-made, pauses when the tokens run out, and picks back up after the reset. Any finds go to Slovenian authorities.

Credit to Gil: https://t.co/YZrNOjvfec

The listing director

Matt built a site that turns property photos into cinematic listing videos.

A civil engineer and videographer, not a developer, Matt used ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude Code to code in real editing rules like kitchens and living rooms staying together, bedrooms sitting next to their bathrooms, and every clip having movement.

Credit to Matt Aromando: https://t.co/cJVDheqEEx

"OpenAI cannot make AI safe on its own."

That's the title of a letter from the three safety researchers OpenAI fired last week, addressed to its safety committees.

OpenAI has said they mishandled confidential information.

One of them, Mikita Balesni, says they were fired for "prioritizing safety over the near-term interests of OpenAI as a corporation." 

Their letter says the firing has "made our former colleagues afraid to speak."

You can just do things with AI, astronomy edition:

Pavel Rabtsevich says he used Claude Code and Codex to find a planet NASA's own software missed in its data for years.

NASA now plans to watch the star closely when its TESS telescope passes over in November. https://t.co/N66EpvhoZV

The Association for Human Mathematics, on OpenAI's 722-paper release: "Mathematicians did not ask for this work to be done."

It also urged mathematicians "to discontinue their work with OpenAI."

Fields Medalist Terence Tao reposted the statement on his blog as a guest post, and X has since run with it as Tao's own words. 

OpenAI has also withdrawn 3 of the papers, and 14 more have been revised since the release.

OpenAI's README on the drop did say that "some of the unformalized results could have issues. We will endeavor to fix any such issues quickly."
